cat.en: Choosing a group and understanding research

q.zh: 大家都說丙組在做 AI，實際研究內容大概是怎麼樣？
q.en: Everyone says Group C does AI. What does the research actually cover?

zh: 丙組的研究範圍其實非常廣。近年的研究從機器學習、LLM、機器人學習、電腦視覺、語音與音樂生成，到生醫資料分析、金融科技、資訊安全、無線與衛星網路、訊號處理，甚至量子資訊與資訊理論都有。不同實驗室做研究的方式差異也很大，有些偏數學與理論分析，有些主要訓練模型、處理大型資料，有些則著重網路與系統實作或跨領域應用。因此如果正在選教授，比起只看「AI、資料科學」這類大標籤，更值得直接看各實驗室近幾年的論文與碩論題目，因為即使都屬於丙組，實際每天做的事情可能完全不同。
en: Group C covers a very broad range of research. Recent work spans machine learning, LLMs, robot learning, computer vision, speech and music generation, biomedical data analysis, financial technology, information security, wireless and satellite networks, signal processing, and even quantum information and information theory. The ways labs conduct research also differ considerably: some emphasize mathematics and theoretical analysis, some mainly train models and work with large datasets, while others focus on networking, system implementation or interdisciplinary applications. If you are choosing an advisor, it is therefore more useful to look directly at each lab’s recent papers and master’s thesis topics than to rely on broad labels such as “AI” or “data science.” Even within Group C, the things you do every day can be completely different.

cat.en: Choosing a group and understanding research

q.zh: 做研究通常是怎樣的流程？和大學修課最大差別在哪？
q.en: What does research involve, and how is it different from undergraduate courses?

zh: 大學修課通常有明確進度、指定教材與標準答案；研究所則是在探索沒有現成解答的問題。常見流程是先閱讀大量相關文獻，找出目前方法還沒解決好的地方，再設計自己的方法、跑實驗、分析結果，最後根據結果反覆修改。
需要適應的通常不是某一門知識特別難，而是研究可能很長一段時間都沒有明確的回饋。方法可能沒有效果、程式可能一直出錯，甚至做到一半才發現別人已經發表類似成果，因此自主找資料、判斷下一步和持續推進的能力會變得很重要。
en: Undergraduate courses usually have a clear schedule, assigned materials and standard answers. Graduate research explores problems without ready-made solutions. A common process is to read extensively, identify what existing methods do not solve well, design your own approach, run experiments, analyze the results, and then revise repeatedly in light of what you find.

The main adjustment is often not that a particular subject is exceptionally difficult, but that research can go for a long time without clear feedback. A method may not work, your code may keep breaking, or you may discover halfway through that someone else has already published a similar result. Finding information independently, deciding what to do next and continuing to make progress become very important.

cat.en: Choosing a group and understanding research

q.zh: 進入丙組需要具備很強的程式能力嗎？
q.en: Do I need to be a very strong programmer to join Group C?

zh: 不用到競賽選手的程度，但如果想走機器學習、電腦視覺或資料相關方向，Python 和主流深度學習框架，例如 PyTorch，最好能熟練使用。
研究通常不是從零開始把所有東西自己寫一遍，而是建立在論文作者或其他研究團隊公開的程式碼上。因此，很核心的一項能力，是能快速看懂 GitHub 上既有專案的結構，知道模型、資料處理、訓練流程分別在哪裡，接著依照自己的研究需求修改模型架構、loss function、資料前處理或實驗設定。讀懂陌生程式碼與 debug 往往更加重要。
en: You do not need to be a competitive programmer. However, if you want to work in machine learning, computer vision or data-related research, it is helpful to be comfortable with Python and mainstream deep-learning frameworks such as PyTorch.

Research usually builds on code released by paper authors or other research teams rather than rewriting everything from scratch. One essential skill is quickly understanding the structure of an unfamiliar GitHub project: locating the model, data processing and training pipeline, then modifying the architecture, loss function, preprocessing or experimental settings for your own research. Reading unfamiliar code and debugging are often even more important.

cat.en: Choosing a group and understanding research

q.zh: 大學時期有必要先做專題嗎？
q.en: Should I do a research project as an undergraduate?

zh: 如果有機會，建議至少做過一次。因為喜歡一門課，不代表一定喜歡做研究。
專題最重要的功能是提早體驗真正的研究過程：讀不熟悉的論文、使用沒學過的工具、自己找問題、實驗失敗後重新調整方向。
en: If you have the opportunity, we recommend doing at least one. Enjoying a course does not necessarily mean you will enjoy research.

The most valuable purpose of an undergraduate project is to experience the actual research process early: reading unfamiliar papers, using tools you have not learned, identifying problems yourself, and adjusting direction after experiments fail.

q.zh: 找教授之前，應該先向學長姐了解哪些資訊？
q.en: What should I ask current students before approaching a professor?

zh: 實驗室網站通常只會寫研究方向，真正影響碩士生活的細節最好直接問在學學長姐。
最值得了解的是老師實際怎麼帶學生，例如多久開一次 meeting、卡關時老師會不會給具體方向，還是希望學生自己摸索；研究題目是老師直接指定計畫，還是讓學生自己找題目；歷屆學生通常多久畢業、是否有論文發表要求；以及平常是否需要固定進實驗室、是否有產學計畫或其他工作需要負責。
另外可以直接問一句：「如果重新選一次，你還會選這個 Lab 嗎？」通常比問「實驗室氣氛好不好」更容易得到有資訊量的答案。當然，也可以很直觀地看看學長姐的眼神還有沒有光。
en: Lab websites usually describe research areas. For the details that will really affect your master’s experience, it is best to ask students who are currently in the lab.

It is especially useful to understand how the professor actually supervises students: how often meetings take place; whether the professor offers concrete direction when you get stuck or expects you to explore independently; whether topics are assigned through projects or developed by students; how long previous students usually took to graduate; whether publication is required; whether regular attendance is expected; and whether you will have industry collaborations or other duties to handle.

You can also ask directly: “If you were choosing again, would you still choose this lab?” That often yields more useful information than “Is the atmosphere good?” And, of course, you can take a very intuitive look at whether the students still have a spark in their eyes.

q.zh: 選 Lab 時，研究題目、指導教授、實驗室風氣該如何權衡？
q.en: How should I weigh the topic, advisor and lab environment?

zh: 如果是碩士班，指導教授的風格與實驗室環境放在研究題目前面。
原因是碩士研究題目常常會隨著研究進度、新論文出現或計畫方向而調整，但教授的指導方式、實驗室文化與工作節奏通常比較固定。題目很喜歡，但和老師溝通方式完全不合，兩年可能會過得很辛苦；反過來，題目不是原本最理想的方向，但教授願意指導、Lab 互動正常，有學長姐照顧可以談心，也可能做得很開心。
所以最好的方式是實際和教授及學長姐談過後決定。
en: For a master’s degree, put the advisor’s mentoring style and the lab environment ahead of the research topic.

Master’s topics often change as research progresses, new papers appear or project directions shift. Mentoring style, lab culture and working rhythm tend to be more stable. You may love a topic, but if you and the professor communicate in completely incompatible ways, those two years can be difficult. Conversely, even if the topic is not your original ideal, a supportive advisor, healthy lab interactions and senior students you can talk to can make the experience enjoyable.
The best approach is to talk with both the professor and current students before deciding.

q.zh: 寄信給教授約面談時，該如何準備？
q.en: How should I prepare an email requesting a meeting with a professor?

zh: 信件不用太長，重點是讓教授快速知道你是誰、為什麼找他，以及你是否真的了解他的研究方向。
可以簡單交代學校、科系、成績與相關經驗，附上一頁履歷與成績單，再指出自己對實驗室哪一個具體研究方向或近期成果有興趣，最後詢問是否方便安排短時間面談。比起寫「我對 AI 很有熱忱」，直接提到一個實驗室正在做的題目會更有說服力。
面談前至少應該看過實驗室最近幾年的研究方向，挑一兩篇論文讀摘要、方法概念與結論。不一定要完全看懂數學細節，但最好能說清楚這篇工作想解決什麼問題，以及為什麼對它有興趣。
en: The email does not need to be long. The point is to help the professor quickly understand who you are, why you are contacting them and whether you actually know their research.

Briefly introduce your university, department, academic performance and relevant experience. Attach a one-page CV and transcript, identify a specific research direction or recent result from the lab that interests you, and ask whether a short meeting would be possible. Mentioning a topic the lab is actually working on is more convincing than simply saying “I am passionate about AI.”

Before the meeting, review the lab’s research directions over the past few years and choose one or two papers whose abstracts, main methodological ideas and conclusions you can read. You do not have to understand every mathematical detail, but you should be able to explain the problem the work addresses and why you find it interesting.

q.zh: 二推進丙組時，有什麼需要特別注意？
q.en: What should I watch out for when entering through a later recommendation round?

zh: 二推最大的現實問題通常不是研究所本身，而是教授名額。
因為時間比較晚，有些熱門實驗室可能已經收了一部分學生，因此錄取之後能選的教授不一定和原本想像的一樣。如果是透過二推進來，建議在決定前先確認目前哪些教授仍可能收學生，以及剩下的研究方向自己是否真的願意做。不要等到錄取後才第一次開始找老師。
en: The main practical issue in a later recommendation round is usually advisor capacity, rather than admission to the institute itself.

Because it happens later, some popular labs may already have accepted students, so the advisors available after admission may differ from what you imagined. Before making a decision through a later round, check which professors might still accept students and whether you would genuinely be willing to work in the remaining research areas. Do not wait until admission to start looking for an advisor for the first time.

q.zh: 大學部先修研究所課程對碩士生活有幫助嗎？
q.en: Does taking graduate courses as an undergraduate help?

zh: 有，而且最直接的好處是減輕碩一的修課負擔。如果能提前抵免部分學分，進入碩士班後就能留下更多完整時間閱讀論文、熟悉實驗室工具與開始研究，不必同時被大量課程和研究進度拉扯。
另一個好處是可以先試水溫。真正修過一門相關研究所課程後，會比只看課名更清楚自己是否喜歡這個方向。如果原本覺得 AI 很有趣，但實際接觸模型、數學與實驗後發現完全不喜歡，也能在正式選研究方向前就調整。
還可以藉由修課提早認識教授，從課堂中了解老師是否符合自己嚮往的風格。
en: Yes. The most direct benefit is reducing your first-year coursework load. If some credits can be transferred in advance, you can preserve longer blocks of time in the master’s program for reading papers, learning lab tools and starting research, instead of being pulled between many courses and research deadlines.

Another benefit is testing the waters. Taking a relevant graduate course gives you a clearer idea of whether you like the area than simply reading its title. If AI initially seems exciting but you discover that you dislike working with the models, mathematics and experiments, you can adjust before formally choosing a research direction.
Courses also let you get to know professors early and observe whether their teaching style fits what you hope for.

q.zh: 如果想走機器學習，丙組自己的課就夠了嗎？
q.en: Are Group C courses enough if I want to study machine learning?

zh: 不一定。機器學習相關課程很多分散在資工、電機、數學等不同系所，有些熱門課程也可能需要加簽。
如果已經確定自己想走 ML 或較偏理論的方向，不要只依照「丙組課表」安排修課，而應該從自己未來研究需要的能力反推，例如機器學習、深度學習、最佳化、機率、線性代數或特定應用領域，再跨系選課。
en: Not necessarily. Machine-learning courses are spread across computer science, electrical engineering, mathematics and other departments, and some popular courses may require an instructor’s enrollment authorization.

If you know you want to pursue ML or a more theoretical direction, do not plan only around the “Group C course list.” Work backward from the abilities your future research will require—for example, machine learning, deep learning, optimization, probability, linear algebra or a particular application domain—and take courses across departments.

q.zh: 碩士期間適合去業界實習嗎？
q.en: Is an industry internship a good idea during a master’s degree?

zh: 如果目標是畢業後直接進業界，實習可以考慮。它可以讓你提前接觸真正的開發流程，也能確認原本想像中的職位，實際做起來是不是自己喜歡的工作。
不過實習前一定要充分跟老師溝通，也要評估自己的研究進度。尤其碩二如果正接近論文關鍵階段，實習可能直接和畢業進度衝突。
en: If you plan to enter industry immediately after graduation, an internship is worth considering. It lets you experience real development workflows and find out whether the role you imagined is actually work you enjoy.

Before taking an internship, however, discuss it thoroughly with your advisor and assess your research progress. In particular, an internship during a critical thesis stage in your second year may directly conflict with your graduation schedule.

q.zh: 丙組畢業後通常可以做哪些工作？
q.en: What kinds of careers can Group C graduates pursue?

zh: 丙組的出路和研究方向連動很大。走機器學習、電腦視覺或語音的人，可能往 AI、演算法或軟體研發發展；做網路、系統或資安的人，則可能進入網路系統、資安或相關研發職位；此外，丙組也有智慧醫療、金融科技等跨領域研究，未來可進一步投入醫療 AI 開發、金融業 AI 應用等工作。訊號處理與其他跨領域應用，也各有對應的產業方向。
因此求職時，「電信丙組」本身通常不是最重要的標籤。企業更容易從你的碩論、專題、修課、實習與技術能力判斷你適合什麼職位。
en: Career paths in Group C depend strongly on the research direction. People working in machine learning, computer vision or speech may pursue AI, algorithm or software R&D roles. Those working on networks, systems or security may enter network systems, cybersecurity or related R&D positions. Group C also includes interdisciplinary research in areas such as smart healthcare and financial technology, which can lead to medical AI development or AI applications in finance. Signal processing and other interdisciplinary applications each have their own corresponding industries.

When looking for a job, “GICE Group C” is therefore usually not the most important label. Employers are more likely to judge your fit through your thesis, projects, coursework, internships and technical abilities.

q.zh: 如果未來想進業界，研究題目要不要刻意選熱門方向？
q.en: Should I deliberately choose a fashionable research topic if I want to work in industry?

zh: 不一定要刻意選熱門題目。
研究所真正重要的訓練，是培養獨立研究、面對問題並解決問題的能力。而在這個過程中累積的模型訓練、資料處理、系統實作、程式工程、文獻閱讀，以及完成大型研究專案的經驗，都能轉移到不同的工作領域——研究題目本身，更像是培養這些能力的「載體」。
企業在評估一個人時，也不只看你做過什麼題目。有些職缺甚至會直接詢問指導教授，了解你在研究所期間的合作表現：是否願意主動承擔沒人想做的工作、執行力如何、遇到問題是否主動解決、是否好相處，以及「如果再選一次，還願不願意收這個學生」。
所以比起追逐當下最熱門的題目，更重要的是在研究所期間，真正培養出獨立解決問題、把事情做完、也能與人合作的能力。
20 幾歲的大家，未來還有很多可能。保持開放、保持彈性、保持謙虛，邊走邊看，一步步解決眼前的問題即可，不必因研究題目過早限制未來。
en: You do not necessarily need to choose a fashionable topic deliberately.

The most important training in graduate school is learning to conduct research independently, face problems and solve them. The model training, data processing, system implementation, software engineering, literature reading and experience of completing a substantial research project that you accumulate can transfer to different fields of work. The topic itself is more like a vehicle for developing these abilities.

Employers do not only look at the topic you studied. Some positions even involve asking your advisor how you worked with others in graduate school: whether you willingly took on tasks nobody else wanted, how effectively you executed, whether you proactively solved problems, whether you were easy to work with, and “If you could choose again, would you still take this student?”
Rather than chasing the hottest topic of the moment, it is more important to develop the ability to solve problems independently, finish what you start and collaborate with others.

In your twenties, many possibilities still lie ahead. Stay open, flexible and humble; learn as you go and solve the problems in front of you step by step. There is no need to let a research topic limit your future too early.
